subject: history
title: Cold War Crises: Cause and Effect
welcome_lead: Today you'll trace the major Cold War crises — Berlin, Cuba and Vietnam — and what each one changed.
meta_desc: GCSE History Cold War crises — Berlin Wall, Cuban Missile Crisis, Vietnam War causes and consequences.
final_note: You can now explain the causes and consequences of the key Cold War crises.

concepts.def: 1948-49 Soviet block of West Berlin supplies
1961 wall sealing off East from West Berlin
Oct 1962 stand-off over Soviet missiles in Cuba
1955-75 US conflict against communist North Vietnam
US policy to stop communism spreading further

walkthroughs.body_html:
In 1948 Stalin blockaded West Berlin. The West replied with the Berlin Airlift — over a year of supply flights.

In August 1961 the East German government built the Berlin Wall to stop East Germans escaping west. It split families for 28 years.

The USSR placed nuclear missiles in Cuba, 90 miles from Florida.

President Kennedy set up a naval blockade in October 1962. After 13 tense days, Khrushchev agreed to remove the missiles. A US-Soviet hotline was set up — both sides had peered over the edge.

The USA fought to stop South Vietnam falling to communism. Despite huge force, the USA withdrew by 1973 and Saigon fell in 1975.

In the 1970s, US-Soviet talks brought detente — arms-control deals (SALT I in 1972) and lower tensions for a while.

mcqs.q: Which Cold War crisis lasted 13 days in October 1962?
Why was the Berlin Wall built in 1961?

numericals.q: In which year did Saigon fall to North Vietnam?
numericals.hint: The final US helicopters left the embassy roof that April.

free_texts.q: What was the US Cold War policy of stopping the spread of communism called? (one word, lowercase)
free_texts.hint: It means holding something back rather than rolling it back.
